q_statement:
The following persons came to India at one time or another:
1. Va-Hien
2. I-Tsing
3. Megasthanes
4, Hieun:Tsang
The correct chronological sequence of their visits is:
explanation:
Exp) Option b is the correct answer.

Chronological sequence of visitors

o Megasthanes: Megasthenes, an ancient Greek historian
and diplomat, arrived in India during the reign of
Chandragupta Maurya, around 300 BCE approximately.
He visited Pataliputra, capital of the Mauryan Empire, and
compiled his observations in the lost work “Indica.” He
described Indian geography and mentioned interactions
with King Sandracottus (Chandragupta Maurya) and
even possibly with King Porus during Alexander the
Great’s invasion.

e Fa-Hien: Faxian (337 CE - c. 422 CE), also known as
Fa-Hien, was a Chinese Buddhist monk and traveler who
journeyed from China to India between 399 and 412 CE to
obtain Buddhist texts. He spent a decade in India during
the reign of Chandragupta II. His travelogue, “A Record
of Buddhist Kingdoms,” provides valuable insights into
early Indian Buddhism. Faxian visited sacred Buddhist
sites and monasteries, including Kapilvastu, Bodh Gaya,
Varanasi, and Kushinagar. He described the prosperity of
Indian cities and their inhabitants’ devotion to Buddhism.

¢ Hieun-Tsang: Hieun-Tsang, born in AL) 602, embarked
on a journey to India in 629 during the Tang Dynasty.
He traveled through perilous terrains and visited
various Indian cities. He admired King Harsha Vardhan’s
patronage of Buddhism in Kannauj. After {6 years, he
returned to China in AD 645, translating Buddhist texts
until his death in AD 664. ,

¢ I-Tsing: Chinese Buddhist traveler I-Tsing journeyed to
India from 671 to 695 A.D. His travelogue ‘Record of the
Inner Law sent home from the Southern Sea’ documents
customs, daily life, and Buddhism’s schools. ‘his valuable
book translates his entire travelogue, offering insights
into Buddhism and I-Tsing’s experiences, along with a
general introduction to the religion.

q_statement: The name by which Ashoka is referred to his inscriptions is:
explanation:
Exp) Option d is the correct answer.

The name by which Ashoka is referred to in his inscriptions
is “Priyadarshi.” Priyadarshi means “One who is liked by
all’. It is generally used in conjunction with Devanampriya
which means “beloved of the Gods”. It reflects Ashoka’s
humility and his dedication to spreading ethical and moral
teachings through his inscriptions. The term “Priyadarshi”
is used in various inscriptions and rock edicts to signify
Ashoka’s commitment to promoting righteous conduct
and his benevolent rule. The various other names of
Ashoka include Buddhashakya and Ashoka (in the Maski
Edict). Dharmasoka (Sarnath inscription), Devanampiya
(meaning beloved of the gods), and Piyadassi (meaning of
pleasing appearance), given in the Sri Lankan Buddhist
chronicles Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa).

explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer.

The Gomateshwara statue is a monolithic statue of Bahubali,
the son of first Tirthankar Rishabhanatha. It is a 60 feet
(18 m) tall statue carved out of a single block of granite. It
is located on Vindhyagiri Hill in Sravanabelegola, in the
Hassan district of Karnataka, India. The statue was built
in the 10th century CE by Chamundraya, a minister of the
Western Ganga dynasty. Chamundraya was a Jain, and he
built the statue as a gesture of his devotion to Bahubali.

enduring impact on later rulers.

Important Tips

Once, there was a wandering monk named Subhadda near

soon, and he wanted to meet him, Subhadda had a question .

he couldn’t answer himself, so he thought Buddha could |

help clear his doubts.

Subhadda decided to visit the sala tree grove where

' Buddha was. He asked Venerable Ananda if he could see
, Buddha. Ananda, however, was concerned about Buddha's
tiredness and told Subhadda not to disturb him.

Subhadda asked the same question two more times, and

each time, Ananda gave the same reply. However, Buddha

overheard part of their conversation and called Ananda
over. He told Ananda to let Subhadda come, saying that

Subhadda’s questions were genuine and that he would —

understand the answers.

So, Subhadda got permission to approach Buddha. After
greeting him, Subhadda mentioned that there were many
other teachers with different teachings. Buddha replied
that Subhadda shouldn’t worry about those teachings and
explained that only where the Noble Eightfold Path exists
can one find those who have reached different levels of
spiritual understanding.
Buddha said that his teaching contains the Noble Eightfold
Path and that only there can one find people at different
levels of understanding. He explained that his teaching
leads to genuine spiritual attainment.
Subhadda then requested to become a monk, and Buddha
agreed, This made Subhadda the last disciple of Buddha,
similar to how Kondanna was the first disciple 45 years
earlier in the deer park at Benares.

pottery, copper tools, and burial practices at Mehrgarh. It

origins and development of the Indus Valley Civilization.

q_statement: The first cereal used by man was:
explanation:
Exp) Option c is the correct answer.
Barley is one of the oldest cereal grains known to be cultivated
by man. It is believed to have been first domesticated in the
Fertile Crescent region of the Middle East around 10,000
years ago. Barley is widely accepted as the first cereal to have
been cultivated by humans around 8000 B.C. Rice and wheat
are considered to have been cultivated later.

q_statement: In the Chalcolithic period people of Maharashtra buried their dead under the floor of their houses in the following orientation:
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer.
As per the archaeological evidence from sites such as Nevasa,
Daimabad, and Inamgaon in Maharashtra, the Chalcolithic
people buried their dead in urns beneath the floor of their
house in the north-to-south position. They did not use
separate cemeteries for this purpose, as was the case with the
Harappans. The burial orientation may reflect some religious

or cultural beliefs of these people, but the exact meaning is
not clear.

q_statement: The compilation of which among the following is based upon the Rig Veda?
explanation:
Exp) Option b is the correct answer
The Samaveda is shortest of all the four Vedas. It is closely
connected with the Rigveda. Samaveda is an independent
collection (Samhita), yet it has taken large number of verses
from Rigveda. These verses are chiefly derived from the
eighth and the ninth Mandalas of the Rigveda. The Samaveda
is compiled exclusively for ritual application, for its verses
are all meant to be chanted at the ceremonies of the Soma-
sacrifice and procedures derived from it.

q_statement: Rajjuka’s were:
c: Feudal Lords in the Gupta empire
explanation:
Exp) Option b is the correct answer.
The Rajukas were officials in the Mauryan administration.
The term “Rajuka” is derived from “rajju,” possibly
referring to land measurement using ropes. Rajukas were
vital Mauryan administrators overseeing districts. They
managed taxation, records, and governance, ensuring
efficient local administration. Their role contributed to
organized governance and revenue collection.
Important Tips
Administrative structure of the Mauryan Empire:
The administrative structure of the Mauryan Empire
featured a hierarchical system that facilitated efficient
governance.

o Provinces and Divisions:

® Provinces were divided into divisions, each
overseen by a Pradeshika. These officials lacked
advisory councils.

¢ Districts and Rajukas:

* Divisions were further divided into districts, led
by Rajukas.

s Rajukas managed local governance, taxation, and
records.

® They were assisted by Yuktas (clerks) for
accounting and secretarial tasks.

> Sub-district Administration:

2 Districts were divided into smaller groups of 5 or
10 villages.

2 Each group was supervised by a Sthanika
responsible for tax collection,

® Gopas supported Sthanikas by maintaining |

accurate records and accounts.
e Village Governance:

: ® The village was the smallest administrative unit, '

led by a Gramini/Gramika.

| * Village decisions were made in consultation with !
Grama-vriddhas, or village elders.
e Overall Structure:

* The Mauryan administrative structure resembled
a pyramid, with the king at the apex and Gramini
at the base.

* Variations in administrative control existed across
different regions, with the central province,
Magadha, under stricter royal supervision.

q_statement: ‘Bhaga’ and ‘Bali’ were:
explanation:
Exp) Option b is the correct answer.

In the context of ancient Indian history, ‘Bhaga and ‘Bali’

referred to sources of revenue.

e Bhaga: In ancient Indian society, “Bhapa” was a term
used to denote a share or portion of the agricultural
produce or wealth that was contributed as revenue or tax,
It was a form of taxation where a certain portion of the
produce or income was collected by the state as revenue.
Normal peasants had to pay one-sixth of the produce
as Bhaga and Sharecroppers, who were given crown
lands and agricultural aid by the state, were required to
contribute fifty percent of their produce as payment to
the government.

¢ Bali: “Bali” referred to offerings or tribute made to the
ruling authority. These offerings could include goods,
produce, or even monetary contributions. Bali was a way
for subjects to acknowledge the authority of the ruler and
provide resources to the administration.

q_statement: ‘Ajivaka’ sect was founded by:
explanation:
Exp) Option c is the correct answer,

The person who started the Ajivika group was Makkali
Gosala. From what we know, Makkali Gosala is the name
linked to this group. He lived around the same time as
Mahavira and Gautam Buddha. The jain texts say that
Makkali Gosala was Mahavira’s student for six years, but
then they went their separate ways, and Gosala started his
own group. During the early days of Jainism and Buddhism,
the Ajivika beliefs were a major competitor. People followed
the Ajivika ideas when the Mauryan Emperor Bindusara
was in charge. He was the father of Emperor Asoka. After
Asoka became a Buddhist, the Ajivika beliefs became less
popular, but they managed to survive for another 1600 years
in places like Tamil Nadu and Karnataka in the southern
parts of India. However, this group finally ended in the 14th
century AD.

q_statement: ‘Ayurveda’ that is ‘Science of Life’ appeared first in:
explanation:
Exp) Option d is the correct answer
The word Ayurveda comes from the word ayur meaning
life and the word veda meaning to know. Ayurveda means
the science of life, and is a medical system practiced in
India, Sri Lanka and Nepal. Ayurveda first appeared in the
Atharvaveda. Most treatments relating to good health and
diseases are available in this vedic book.

Important Tips

Upa-Veda

q_statement: Who established ‘Rajdharma’ on triplex bases of longanimity, liberty and compassion?
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer.

Rajdharma is a Sanskrit term that means “the duty ofa king. It
includes subjects’ welfare, security, justice, and maintaining
the social order. The one who established ‘Rajdharma’ based
on the principles of forbearance, freedom, and compassion
was Ashoka. After a period of conquest and warfare, Ashoka,
the Mauryan emperor, embraced Buddhism and adopted a
policy of non-violence and benevolence. His policy aimed
at ruling with a sense of moral responsibility towards his
subjects, promoting religious tolerance, and ensuring the
welfare of his people through compassion and equitable
governance.

q_statement: In the Rigvedic period, people believed mainly in-
explanation:
Exp) Option d is the correct answer

The Early Vedic people followed a simple mode of worship.
They worshipped the forces of nature such as the “Sun, the
Fire, the Wind, the Dawn, the Water, the Rain God Indra,
and Earth”. Their religion primarily consisted of some form
of obligations and prayers. The Vedic people chanted hymns
to praise their Gods. They also performed certain ritual
sacrifices known as yajnas to please their Gods.

q_statement: In the ancient period chief-livelihood source of the Aryans was-
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer

The Aryans pursued pastoralism and agriculture as the
main source of their livelihood. They cleared new land for
cultivation where they produced wheat, barley, and rice.
They also produced other products like cotton and oil seeds.
Irrigation facilities were developed with wells and canals.

q_statement: The beginning of idol worship is to be considered in-
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer

Idol workship in India can be traced to the period of Pre -
Aryans. The Indus Valley people seemed to have a tradition
of honoring their deities in image form with ritual worship.
‘They also probably worshipped animals , mythical creatures ,
plants , kings and gods who resembled humans. In pre Aryan
period most people practised the worshipping idols (pooja)
of mother goddesses, Pahupati seal or animist spirits like
that of wild boar, elephant, and cobra.

q_statement: The Great Bath was found from the Indus Valley civilization at-
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer

Great Bath, ancient structure at Mohenjo-daro, Pakistan, an
archaeological site featuring ruins of the Indus civilization.
The Great Bath dates to the 3rd millennium BCE and is
believed to have been used for ritual bathing. The Great Bath
was a large rectangular tank in a courtyard surrounded by
a corridor on all four sides. There were two flights of steps
on the north and south leading into the tank, which was
made watertight by setting burnt bricks on edge and using a
mortar of gypsum. There were rooms on three sides, in one
of which was a large well, Water from the tank flowed into a
huge drain. Across a lane to the north lay a smaller building
with eight bathrooms, four on each side of a corridor, with

drains from cach bathroom connecting fo a drain that ran

along the corridor. The uniqueness of the structure is that it

is located at the Citadel, this has led scholars to suggest that

it was meant for some kind of a special ritual bath.

q_statement: The standing statue of Gautam Buddha was built in which period?
explanation:
Exp) Option b is the correct answer.

The standing statue of Gautama Buddha was built in the

Kushana period, which lasted from the Ist to the 3rd

centuries CE. It is located in Sarnath, Varanasi, Uttar

Pradesh. The standing statue of Gautama Buddha is one of

the most famous examples of Kushana Buddhist art. It is

a large sculpture that is made of sandstone. The statue is

depicted as the Buddha standing with his right hand raised

in the Abhaya Mudra, which is a gesture of fearlessness. The

statue is thought to have been originally located in a stupa,

or Buddhist shrine.

q_statement: The important reason to keep Indus- Valley civilization before Aryan civilization is-
explanation:
Exp) Option d is the correct answer

One of the key reasons why archacologists believe that the

Indus Valley Civilization{JVC) should be placed before the

Aryan Civilization is the evidence of pottery. ‘The earliest

pottery found in the IVC is dated to around 3300 BCE, while

the earliest pottery found in association with the Aryans is

dated to around 1500 BCE. This suggests that the IVC was

already well established by the time the Aryans arrived in the

Indian subcontinent.

q_statement: Deimachus came to India during the reign of-
explanation:
Exp) Option b is the correct answer.

Deimachus, a Greek from Plataeae, who lived during the

third-century BCE, came to India during the reign of

Bindusara, the Mauryan ruler. He served as an ambassador

to the Mauryan court in Pataliputra. Deimachus was sent

by Antiochus I Soter, and he succeeded the renowned

ambassador Megasthenes. Both Deimachus and Megasthenes

wrote extensively about India, although their works are now

lost. They provided various accounts of India’s geography

and culture, some of which were considered fanciful or

exaggerated.

q_statement: Mahaparinirvana Temple is located at-
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer.

The Mahaparinirvana Temple is located in Kushinagar,

Uttar Pradesh, India. It is said to be the place where the

Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana, or the final passing

away. The temple was built in the 5th century AD by Swami

Haribala, a disciple of the Buddha. It is a large complex with

a number of shrines and stupas. The main shrine houses a

q_statement: India’s first hospital and herbal gardens were built by?
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer.

India’s first hospital and herbal gardens were established

by Ashoka, the Mauryan emperor. Ashoka’s interest

in healthcare and well-being is evident from his edicts,
particularly the Rock Edict No. 2. In this edict, Ashoka
emphasizes the importance of providing medical care to
both humans and animals. He directed the establishment
of hospitals, medical dispensaries, and medical treatment
centers across his empire. These institutions were meant
to provide medical aid, treatment, and care to the sick and
injured,

q_statement: Which of the following sites has yielded skeleton of the dog along with human skeleton in burial?
explanation:
Exp) Option b is the correct answer.
Burzahom is the site that has yielded skeleton of the dog
along with human skeleton in burial. Burzahom is a Neolithic
site located in the Kashmir Valley, where people practiced
agriculture, animal domestication, and pottery making.
Some of the burials at Burzahom show that dogs were buried
with humans, possibly as companions or guardians in the
afterlife. One of the burials even shows a dog skeleton placed
between two human skeletons, as if to protect them]. This
indicates that dogs and humans had a close relationship in
this culture.

Important Tips a

« Brahmagiri: This is a site in Karnataka where
megalithic monuments have been found, dating from
the 2nd millennium BCE to the early historical period.
Some of the burials at Brahmagiri were made in urns, ;
cists, or dolmens. One skeleton was buried with 33 gold
beads, 2 stone beads, 4 copper bangles and one conch
shell

e Chirand: This is an archaeological site in Bihar,
situated on the northern bank of the Ganga River. It
has a large pre-historic mound which is known for its

continuous archacological record from the Neolithic
age (about 2500-1345 BCE) to the reign of the Pal
dynasty who ruled during the pre-medieval period.
The excavations in Chirand have revealed stratified
Neolithic, Chalcolithic, and Iron Age settlements, and
transitions in human habitation patterns.

in Karnataka, where an Ashokan rock edict was
discovered in 1915. It dates back to the 3rd century
BCE and contains the name Ashoka in it instead of the !
earlier edicts that referred him as Devanampriya or
Beloved -of-the-Gods 4}

been recovered from the site of Kalibangan. The meaning of
the horned deity on a terracotta cake is not fully understood.
Some scholars believe that it represents a fertility god, while
